question.worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $4$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{5x-4}{4x+3}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{5x-4}{4(x+\frac{3}{4})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{5x-4}{(x+\frac{3}{4})}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

|  | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $-\frac{3}{4}$ | $5$ | $-4$ |
|  | $↓$ | $-\frac{15}{4}$ |
|  | $5$ | $-\frac{31}{4}$ |

So, from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5x-4}{(x+\frac{3}{4})} & =5-\frac{(\frac{31}{4})}{(x+\frac{3}{4})} \\  & =5-\frac{31}{4x+3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{5x-4}{4x+3}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}(5-\frac{31}{4x+3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[5{\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}x-31{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{4x+3}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{[5x-\frac{31}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|4x+3|]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[5(2-0)-\frac{31}{4}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|11|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|3|)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[10-\frac{31}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{11}{3})] \\  & =\frac{5}{2}-\frac{31}{16}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{11}{3}).\end{aligned}
$$
